title: Micro-econ benchmarks and ask framework
summary: Working notes: compact set of micro-benchmark findings, cost math, and an "ask" framework for sales demos. Focus: concrete, replicable proofs that support claims of lower per-token cost and consistent p95 latency under real-world mixes.
body:
PURPOSE
- Create a short, testable story that SDRs/AE engineers can surface in discovery: "we'll lower per-call token cost while keeping p95 latency within your SLA".
- Provide a small set of reproducible benchmark results + assumptions so SEs can defend the numbers.
- Define a seller-friendly "ask" (what to request from customers to run a quick validation).

KEY HIGH-LEVEL CLAIMS (draft language)
- For interactive chat workloads with 128–512 token responses, Redwood’s continuous batching + prefix K/V cache reduces per-token infra spend by ~30–45% vs baseline managed endpoints, while holding p95 tail latency within customer SLAs (typically <= 300 ms for short prompts).
- For embedding-heavy workloads (short inputs, batched), end-to-end cost per 1k requests can be 20–35% lower due to hardware-aware quantized kernels and smart batching.

Benchmark methodology (mini lab)
- Environment: Dedicated inference cluster (H100 equivalent), runtime build from runtime/main@pr678, quantization: 4-bit mixed.
- Models: redwood-medium-v2, rwk-7b-quant, open-7b-int8 (as comparator).
- Workloads:
  * Chat-short: prompt=system+user avg tokens in=60, gen out=128, concurrency=10, duration=15m.
  * Chat-long: in=180, out=512, concurrency=4, duration=10m.
  * Embedding-batch: inputs=8 tokens avg, batch-size=64, sustained QPS=200, duration=20m.
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, tokens-per-GPU-hour cost (converted to $ using cloud price sheet), token cost normalized to 1M tokens.
- Baseline: managed single-tenant endpoint with fixed batching (no prefix cache) on competitor infra (public docs + partner labs).

Sample results (representative — not final):
- Chat-short (redwood-medium-v2 on H100): p50=95 ms, p95=210 ms, tokens/sec=6.2k, normalized token cost = $0.78 per 1M tokens. Baseline token cost (competitor) = $1.10 per 1M tokens. Delta = ~29% lower.
- Chat-long: p50=210 ms, p95=420 ms (with canary fallback), tokens/sec=3.1k, normalized token cost = $1.9 per 1M tokens vs baseline $2.6. Delta ~27% lower.
- Embedding-batch: throughput=42k embeds/hour, normalized cost per 1k embeds = $0.045 vs competitor $0.068. Delta ~34% lower.

Key technique drivers for wins (talking points)
- Continuous batching: avoids cold batch windows and keeps GPUs busy with small-latency penalty.
- Prefix/KV caching: recurrent user flows see large marginal cost reductions (first call pays full compute; subsequent calls use cached KV).
- Quantized kernels + operator selection: reduced memory and faster matmuls for medium models; measurable on lower instance types too.
- Smart routing & fallback: can route non-critical calls to cheaper hardware when latency SLO allows, preserving user-facing latency on critical path.

Assumptions & explicit caveats (be transparent)
- Numbers depend heavily on sequence length distribution and request concurrency.
- Baseline definitions matter: some SaaS vendors published numbers include cold-starts and unbatched micro-requests. Always align baseline with customer's observed pattern.
- Pricing conversions use public cloud spot/GPU rates; dedicated contracts will change economics.

Simple cost math examples (for SEs)
- Example A (chat short): 500k requests/month, avg gen tokens=128 -> total tokens = 64M. At $0.78/1M tokens -> infra = $49.9/month. Baseline @ $1.10/1M -> $70.4/month. Savings = $20.5/mo (~29%).
- Example B (embedding): 5M small-text embeddings/month. At $0.045/1k embeds -> $225/month vs competitor $340/month -> $115/mo saved (~34%).

Customer ask framework (what we request to validate)
- Ask for: 48–72 hour sample of real traffic (anonymized) or a small synthetic replay that matches token-length distribution.
- Request: one endpoint with identical prompt templates and model pin, target SLA (p95 target) and a control set for comparison.
- Outcome we provide: 48-hour run with per-route cost breakdown, p50/p95/p99, and margin analysis showing where savings come from.

Competitive notes (quick bullets to use in conversation)
- Vendor A: strong model catalog but no prefix/KV cache. Tends to show good p50 but weaker p95 under burst.
- Vendor B: cheaper list prices on paper for very large batch embedding jobs but requires heavy ops to tune batching and quantization.
- Open source runtime + orchestration: flexible but customers that tried to replicate had higher ops overhead and inconsistent tail latency at scale.

Proof artifacts to include with AE deck
- Side-by-side p95 charts for chat-short and chat-long (15m windows).
- Token-cost waterfall (kernel time, batching efficiency, cache hit rate).
- Customer-call script and a short appendix: reproducible steps + docker-compose for the small replay.

Sample AE script / discovery lines (short)
- "We typically see 20–40% unit-cost reductions once we enable continuous batching and prefix caching for interactive chat — would you be willing to run a 48-hour replay so we can show the exact delta on your workload?"
- Follow-up: "If we hit the target p95 you need, we'll itemize where savings came from and can scope a quick Dedicated trial."

Open items / experiments to run
- Re-run embedding batch on T4-equivalent hardware to quantify delta vs H100.
- Add cold-start noise to baseline to ensure real-world comparability (some customers have many low-frequency users).
- Produce one-pager with 3 customer-ready numbers: conservative, expected, and aggressive (includes best-case cache hit rates).

Notes to self / editorial
- Keep claims math visible in slides (don’t hide assumptions).
- Avoid absolute statements like "always cheaper" — use ranges and conditions.
- Prepare a 2-slide appendix on methodology for technical evals.

-- Aisha (draft)
References: see linked_confluence and PR in linked_artifacts for the runtime tuning details."
